seo.title: Best Tools for AI Development in 2026
seo.description: Top AI development tools for LLM integration, vector databases, prompt engineering, and AI-powered coding. Curated by engineers building AI products.

introduction: AI has moved from experimental to essential in software development — both as a tool developers use and as a capability they build into products. The landscape of AI development tools is evolving weekly, making it hard to know what's battle-tested versus hype. At GEXP Software, we integrate AI capabilities into client applications and use AI tools in our own workflow. These are the tools that deliver real value.

categories.name: LLM SDKs & Frameworks
categories.description: Libraries and frameworks for integrating large language models into applications with structured output, streaming, and tool use.

items.name: Vercel AI SDK
items.description: Unified TypeScript SDK for building AI-powered applications with React Server Components and streaming UI. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 20+ providers through a single API.
items.highlight: Stream AI responses directly into React Server Components

items.name: LangChain.js
items.description: JavaScript framework for building LLM applications with chains, agents, and RAG pipelines. Provides abstractions for common AI patterns while maintaining flexibility for custom implementations.

items.name: Instructor
items.description: Library for extracting structured data from LLMs using Zod schemas. Define the shape of your output in TypeScript and get validated, typed responses every time — no prompt parsing needed.
items.highlight: Define output schema with Zod — get validated structured data

items.name: Anthropic SDK
items.description: Official TypeScript SDK for Claude with streaming, tool use, and vision capabilities. Clean API design with full type safety for building applications powered by Claude models.

items.name: OpenAI SDK
items.description: Official Node.js library for the OpenAI API with streaming, function calling, and assistants support. The most widely-used LLM SDK with extensive documentation and examples.

items.name: Mastra
items.description: TypeScript framework for building AI agents and workflows with built-in tool calling, memory, and evaluation. Designed for production agent systems, not just chat interfaces.
items.highlight: Production-ready AI agent framework with built-in evaluation

categories.name: Vector Databases & RAG
categories.description: Vector storage, embedding, and retrieval augmented generation tools for building knowledge-powered AI applications.

items.name: Pinecone
items.description: Managed vector database purpose-built for AI applications with sub-100ms query latency at any scale. Handles embedding storage, similarity search, and metadata filtering without infrastructure management.
items.highlight: Sub-100ms vector search at billion-scale with zero infrastructure

items.name: Chroma
items.description: Open-source embedding database that runs in-memory, locally, or in the cloud. The simplest way to add vector search to your application — pip install and go.
items.highlight: Runs embedded in your app — no external service needed

items.name: Supabase pgvector
items.description: Vector similarity search built into Supabase's PostgreSQL using the pgvector extension. Store embeddings alongside your application data without adding another database.
items.highlight: Vector search in your existing Postgres — no new database

items.name: LlamaIndex
items.description: Data framework for connecting LLMs with your private data through indexing, retrieval, and query engines. Ingests documents, builds indexes, and answers questions over your knowledge base.

items.name: Unstructured
items.description: Document processing library that extracts text and metadata from PDFs, images, HTML, Word docs, and 30+ file formats. The preprocessing step that makes RAG pipelines actually work with real-world documents.
items.highlight: Extract clean text from any document format for RAG pipelines

categories.name: AI-Powered Coding Tools
categories.description: Tools that use AI to assist with code writing, review, debugging, and development workflows.

items.name: Claude Code
items.description: Anthropic's agentic coding tool that operates directly in your terminal. Reads your codebase, makes multi-file changes, runs tests, and handles complex refactoring tasks autonomously.
items.highlight: Agentic coding in your terminal with full codebase context

items.name: GitHub Copilot
items.description: AI pair programmer that suggests code completions, entire functions, and test cases as you type. Integrated into VS Code, JetBrains, and Neovim with workspace-aware context.

items.name: Cursor
items.description: AI-native code editor built on VS Code with deep LLM integration. Features include codebase-aware chat, multi-file editing, and a compose mode that lets AI make changes across your project.

items.name: Codeium / Windsurf
items.description: Free AI code completion and chat with support for 70+ languages. The Windsurf editor adds agentic capabilities with cascading actions that handle multi-step coding tasks.

items.name: Aider
items.description: Terminal-based AI pair programmer that edits your local files with git integration. Supports multiple LLMs and automatically creates git commits for every change it makes.
items.highlight: Auto-commits every AI change with meaningful messages

categories.name: Prompt Engineering & Evaluation
categories.description: Tools for designing, testing, versioning, and evaluating LLM prompts and AI application outputs.

items.name: Langfuse
items.description: Open-source LLM observability platform for tracing, evaluating, and debugging AI applications. See every prompt, completion, latency, and cost in a detailed trace view.
items.highlight: Full trace visibility for every LLM call — prompts, completions, costs

items.name: Braintrust
items.description: AI evaluation and observability platform with human and AI-powered scoring, dataset management, and prompt playground. Ship AI features with confidence using systematic evaluation.
items.highlight: Systematic AI evaluation with human and automated scoring

items.name: Helicone
items.description: LLM proxy and observability layer that sits between your app and the LLM provider. Adds caching, rate limiting, cost tracking, and analytics without changing your code.

items.name: Promptfoo
items.description: Open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM prompts systematically. Define test cases, run them against multiple models, and compare results side-by-side in a web UI.
items.highlight: Compare prompt performance across models side-by-side

items.name: LangSmith
items.description: LangChain's platform for debugging, testing, and monitoring LLM applications. Provides production-grade tracing with detailed latency breakdowns for every chain and agent step.

categories.name: AI Infrastructure & Deployment
categories.description: Tools for deploying, serving, and managing AI models and AI-powered applications in production.

items.name: Ollama
items.description: Run open-source LLMs locally with a simple command-line interface. Download and run Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and dozens of other models on your machine for development and testing.
items.highlight: Run Llama, Mistral, and other LLMs locally with one command

items.name: Replicate
items.description: Cloud platform for running open-source AI models via API. Run Stable Diffusion, Whisper, LLaMA, and thousands of other models without managing GPU infrastructure.

items.name: Hugging Face
items.description: The central hub for AI models, datasets, and spaces. Host models, share datasets, and deploy ML applications. Its Transformers.js library brings model inference directly to the browser.
items.highlight: Largest open-source AI model hub with 500K+ models

items.name: Together AI
items.description: Fast inference platform for open-source LLMs with OpenAI-compatible API. Run Llama, Mixtral, and other models at scale with competitive pricing and low latency.

items.name: Modal
items.description: Serverless cloud for running GPU workloads — fine-tuning, batch inference, and custom model serving. Write Python functions and they run on GPUs in the cloud with automatic scaling.
items.highlight: Serverless GPU functions — deploy with a Python decorator
